program.merge_policy: accumulate twenty 25-finding passes; consolidate, admit, validate, and merge once after Wave 1500

source_provenance: collision screening against merged history, pending Waves 501-1000, and active Waves 1001-1350

policy.validation_strategy: PMID-level dedupe/source verification during authoring; expensive repository-wide validation only after Wave 1500

waves.focus: Four-month randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial in 198 male shift workers found vitamin D raised serum 25(OH)D but did not reduce central adiposity; biomarker correction did not translate into an obesity benefit.

DANCODE multicenter double-blind randomized trial found vitamin K2 plus D3 slowed severe coronary-calcification progression over 24 months, but the imaging effect does not establish fewer cardiovascular events.

TARGET-D randomized trial found titrated vitamin D management after myocardial infarction did not significantly reduce major adverse cardiovascular events; one recurrent-MI secondary signal does not overturn the primary null.
Randomized winter feeding trial found 25(OH)D3-biofortified chicken and eggs prevented seasonal vitamin-D decline, but standard vitamin D3 supplementation increased serum 25(OH)D more.

Network meta-analysis of 21 prediabetes RCTs produced different dose rankings across glycemic outcomes; indirect comparisons and sparse low-dose evidence make apparent optimal-dose signals exploratory.

Twelve-month randomized four-arm trial in older adults with MCI found vitamin D3, DHA and their combination improved selected cognitive and pyroptosis measures, with the combination appearing stronger; combination superiority needs independent replication.

VITAL secondary analysis found neither vitamin D3 nor marine omega-3 significantly reduced selected Alzheimer-related plasma biomarkers over four years; subgroup signals were uncorrected and hypothesis-generating.
Short randomized double-blind trial found vitamin D changed selected inflammatory responses but did not improve repeated Wingate anaerobic performance.
Meta-analysis of five randomized trials found vitamin D supplementation did not reduce melanoma incidence or recurrence; randomized evidence is currently neutral.

Meta-analysis of vitamin D plus probiotic/synbiotic co-supplementation found a modest fasting-insulin signal while HOMA-IR, glucose, lipids and anthropometrics were null overall; combination evidence remains limited.

Randomized placebo-controlled trial in premenopausal women with benign breast disease found cholecalciferol improved selected insulin-sensitivity indices but not fasting glucose, lipids or anthropometrics between groups.

Triple-blind pediatric trial found within-group metabolic improvements during omega-3/omega-9 interventions, but intervention assignment did not independently predict response and between-group differences were absent.
Tiny randomized phase-II pilot found curcumin plus omega-3 was well tolerated but did not significantly change primary pulmonary-nodule imaging endpoints; no chemopreventive efficacy was established.

Double-blind randomized trial in young children with autism found omega-3/omega-6 supplementation had no overall effect on cytokines or autism-related behaviors; sex-specific findings were exploratory.
Systematic review and meta-analysis found no clear benefit of isolated omega-3 supplementation on fat-free mass or muscle strength in healthy adults, with very-low-certainty evidence.

Updated randomized-trial meta-analysis found small statistical improvements in irritability and communication but no significant effects across several other autism behavioral domains; clinical relevance remains uncertain.
Systematic review/meta-analysis found no significant pooled benefit of adjunctive omega-3 on PANSS total, clinical response or discontinuation outcomes in schizophrenia.
Quasi-randomized pilot found omega-3 changed whole-blood EPA/DHA and fatty-acid ratios but did not improve patient-reported migraine pain, disability or distress.
Randomized pharmacokinetic comparison of liposomal and non-liposomal omega-3 formulations informs formulation/exposure differences, not clinical superiority.
Randomized double-blind trial after total hip arthroplasty found hydrolyzed collagen did not alter postoperative bone-turnover biomarkers versus placebo; one pain signal was secondary.
Small randomized crossover study found fava-bean protein altered thermoregulatory and intestinal-damage markers during exercise in heat but did not improve graded exercise time or GI symptoms.

Secondary analysis of a triple-blind RCT found resistance training improved strength across groups while whey protein reduced HOMA-IR without significant HbA1c, fasting-glucose, lipid or hypertrophy benefits.

Twelve-week randomized trial found almonds did not improve the primary anxiety/depression score or microbiome/SCFA outcomes versus control, though stool hardness and some functional-impairment analyses favored almonds.

Meta-analysis of 18 RCTs found no meaningful long-term differences between plant- and animal-protein supplementation in body composition, strength, physical performance or major cardiometabolic risk factors when protein intake was adequate.

Very small randomized crossover trial found pre-sleep whey improved several sleep measures and next-day soreness versus isocaloric control but not consistently versus casein; the result is preliminary.
